subject.title: [Bug]: Successful Discord source reply can be sent again after native Codex compaction in the same turn

question: Should the Codex source-reply contract preserve a turn-scoped committed-delivery marker across compaction, and what explicit signal distinguishes a valid subsequent progress/update send from a duplicate final reply?
rationale: The intended fix must prevent duplicate visible replies without turning every successful message-tool call into a terminal or globally one-shot action, which conflicts with the adjacent progress-send behavior reports.

options.title: Preserve delivery state with explicit follow-ups
options.body: Carry committed source-delivery state through compaction and require an explicit distinct/progress delivery intent for any later source send in the same turn.

options.title: Treat first source send as terminal
options.body: End source-reply turns after the first successful send, accepting the loss of same-turn progress and follow-up delivery behavior.

options.title: Defer contract change
options.body: Keep the existing behavior until a deterministic reproduction and native Codex protocol audit identify a narrower implementation boundary.

recommendation.title: Preserve delivery state with explicit follow-ups
recommendation.body: Carry committed source-delivery state through compaction and require an explicit distinct/progress delivery intent for any later source send in the same turn.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available low-confidence routing candidate for a cross-runtime behavior contract rather than a Discord-adapter-only change.
